messages:
Alex: :wave: Nightwatch here — quick pre-handoff check. I’m stepping off in 10m. Need to confirm primary/secondary for APAC window tomorrow and validate that PD/Grafana/AWS access is green. Planning to mark Priya primary, Sam secondary unless either of you flag an issue.
Priya: I can take primary for the 00:00-08:00 UTC slice. :thumbsup: Quick note — I lost Grafana dashboard access earlier (got a lock icon). Could be a role drift.
Sam: I’m happy to be secondary. I still have full PagerDuty responder role but can’t assume the "oncall-ops" IAM role via SSO right now — getting an error when running the assume-role script.
Alex: Thanks. Sam, paste the exact error? If it’s the SSO token expiry we can re-auth. If it’s an IAM change we should escalate.
Sam: Error: "AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/oncall-ops". Happened after a laptop reboot.
Marta: tagging infra — @devops-bot can you check if the oncall-ops role trust policy was edited in the last 24h? Also we have a runbook for access checks: https://runbooks.redwood.com/oncall/access-checklist (useful to walk through).
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20250412-298 — "role-assume-fail"; severity: low; assigned: infra. Links: https://incidents.redwood.com/INC-20250412-298
Alex: Ok, follow checklist while infra looks at role policy. Priya — can you confirm PagerDuty and Grafana roles? Steps to verify you can run: ```# PagerDuty: check schedules
pd schedules list --user priya@redwood.com
# Grafana: open org settings -> users -> find your email
# AWS: aws sts get-caller-identity && aws iam simulate-principal-policy --principal-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/priya@redwood.com --action-names sts:AssumeRole
```
Priya: PagerDuty shows me as Responder for the oncall schedule. Grafana shows Editor role for org "redwood-prod". AWS sts get-caller-identity succeeds; simulate-principal-policy shows Allow for AssumeRole on oncall-ops.
Sam: I retried after re-login to SSO and now assume-role works. Looks like my cached SSO session expired on reboot. :man_facepalming: Confirming I can access Grafana and PD too.
Alex: Great. Two action items: 1) Infra please confirm no policy drift on role (INC-20250412-298). 2) Priya/Sam/Alex — if you hit lock icon in Grafana, try incognito to rule out cached cookies; if persists open a Grafana permissions ticket and include the dashboard id.
Marta: infra confirms no recent edits to the role trust policy; incident updated. Looks like transient SSO expiry for Sam. Marking INC-20250412-298 as resolved (root cause: client SSO token expired).
devops-bot: Change log: no iam:update_role or trust policy changes in last 72h. Audit-ids: a1b2c3.
Alex: Closing checklist. Final run-through before handoff: Primary: Priya (confirmed PD/Grafana/AWS), Secondary: Sam (confirmed), Slack bridge oncall channel notifications enabled, runbook link pinned here: https://runbooks.redwood.com/oncall/incident-response. If either of you need temporary elevation, please request via the Access Slack workflow (/request-access) with the incident id.
Priya: Got it — I’ll take the bridge at 00:00 UTC. Thanks Alex.
Sam: Standing by as secondary. :ok_hand:
Alex: Thanks team — handoff complete. :lock:
